##: dispatches to from the msi leg of its release workflow. version, url and hash
are the only three fields it rewrites; everything else here is edited by hand.
The url names a release asset of stepss-java-ui. That name is a contract
between the two repositories: rename the asset there and every release cut
afterwards stops resolving here, while older tags stay un-resyncable because
the new name never existed on them.
description: Static and Transient Electric Power Systems Simulation: dynamic simulation, power flow and small-signal stability analysis of electric power systems
post_install: # Scoop creates Start Menu entries only, under 'Scoop Apps'. The Windows
# installer also puts an icon on the desktop, and this route should not be
# the poor relation, so the desktop shortcut is made here by hand.
# $dir is the 'current' junction rather than the versioned directory:
# link_current runs before post_install, so this shortcut keeps working
# across updates instead of pointing into a directory the next release
# deletes. IconLocation is set explicitly rather than left to the target's
# own resources, so that a build which somehow shipped without STEPSS.ico
# is caught here and in the shortcuts entry above rather than showing a
$link.Description = 'Static and Transient Electric Power Systems Simulation'
pre_uninstall: # Runs on update too, before the old version is torn down, and post_install
# then makes the shortcut again. Only a shortcut that points into this
# Scoop app is removed: one of the same name left by the MSI installer, or
# made by the user, is theirs and not ours to delete.
notes: STEPSS is installed under your own profile and needs no administrator rights.
It is on the Start Menu under 'Scoop Apps', on your desktop, and on PATH as 'stepss'.
